Rashi on Eruvin 3a:10:1.english: Why do they need - the Rabbis and R. Yehuda to disagree about two matters?

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:11:1.english: A mavoi for walking is made - That is to say, the one walking does not look upward:

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:12:1.english: Kinnei - For example, bird nests that jutted out from beneath the portico, above the doorway (Mel'):

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:12:2.hebrew: פסקי דארזא - כלונסות של ארז ארוכין תחובין בכותל, ואיידי דנפיש משכיה אורך דידהו חזו להו אינשי ואיכא היכרא:
Rashi on Eruvin 3a:12:2.english: Pisḳei d'Arza - Long cedar stakes inserted into the wall; and because their length was great, people would see them, and they served as a distinguishing mark:

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:13:1.english: The one who says “pesakim” - there is a distinguishing mark for the alleyway.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:13:2.hebrew: כל שכן קיני - דאיידי דחשיבי ומילתא דתמיהא היא, מסתכלי בהו אינשי וחזו לקורה:
Rashi on Eruvin 3a:13:2.english: All the more so nests - Because it is a noteworthy and astonishing matter, people look at them and see the beam:

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:16:1.hebrew: מקצת - עובי הקורה בתוך כ' ומקצתה למעלה, וכן עובי סככה של סוכה:
Rashi on Eruvin 3a:16:1.english: Part - The thickness of a beam within [a height of] twenty [amot], and part of it above; and likewise the thickness of the covering (sekhakh) of a sukkah:

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:17:1.english: Kalush (thin / pared down) - We regard it as though the protruding thickness above has been removed, so that it becomes a thin beam.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:19:1.hebrew: הניטלת ברוח - שהרי שיערוה חכמים בריאה כדי לקבל אריח, ואי לאו הכי שדי ליה זיקא, הלכך לא חשיב:
Rashi on Eruvin 3a:19:1.english: Carried off by the wind - Since the Sages assessed it as strong enough to bear a tile; otherwise, the wind would carry it away, so it is not considered [a proper roof beam].

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:1:1.hebrew: לא תיהני ליה אמלתרא - לאכשורי גובהו יותר מכ', לקמן מפרש מאי אמלתרא והיכא תני דמהניא:
Rashi on Eruvin 3a:1:1.english: The amaltara should not help it - to validate its height [when it is] more than twenty [cubits]. Below [the Gemara] explains what amaltara is, and where [the mishna] teaches that it helps.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:1:2.english: Of gall-nut - A tree on which galls grow; they are afatzim [oak galls], and in the vernacular [Old French]: gales.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:20:1.hebrew: לא מידכר - וזמנין דמשתקיל מקצת עובי הסכך הנכנס לתוך כ', וקיימא כולה למעלה מכ':
Rashi on Eruvin 3a:20:1.english: Is not mentioned - Sometimes some of the thickness of the covering that enters within twenty [cubits] is made light [i.e., disregarded], and all of it remains above twenty.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:20:2.english: Mentioning each other - That is, if the bottom of a beam rotted and the entire beam stood above twenty cubits, one may repair it:

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:24:1.english: But - Why is it fit for a sukkah? Because necessarily its shade is now greater than its sun, since [the Gemara] speaks of seeing [the sky through its covering], and we do not subtract anything from it.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:24:2.hebrew: הכא נמי - חשוב אותה כשפודין כבידין, דאי נמי קלישי לא שדי להו זיקא, דהא לא מידי שקלת מינה, אלא רואין הוא דקאמר:
Rashi on Eruvin 3a:24:2.english: Here too - Consider it as heavy posts, for even if they were thin, the wind would not carry them off. Since you did not take anything from the sukkah, but rather [the Gemara] is speaking of [the beam] being seen:

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:4:1.english: Why then did Rabbi Ile'a say, etc.? - Now [the Gemara] is bringing its rebuttal to a conclusion — [demonstrating] that we have found that the amaltara is effective according to Rav. But at the outset [the Gemara] did not allow [the questioner] to complete his statement until it had refuted his objection.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:4:2.hebrew: רחבה ד' - אם היתה קורה רחבה ד' טפחים, אע"פ שהיא דקה ואינה חזקה לקבל אריח, כשירה. והא דתנן במתניתין (לקמן עירובין ד' יג:) בריאה כדי לקבל אריח, כשאינה רחבה ד' טפחים קאמר:
Rashi on Eruvin 3a:4:2.english: Wide four [handbreadths] - If the beam was four handbreadths wide, even though it is thin and not strong enough to hold a half-brick, it is valid. And that which we learned in the Mishna (later, Eruvin 13b): "[the beam must be] sturdy enough to hold a half-brick" — that is speaking when it is not four handbreadths wide.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:4:3.english: And if it has an amaltera, etc. - Rav is stating two things, and [both are] leniencies.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:5:1.hebrew: אמר רב יוסף - הא אמלתרא דאייתוה משמיה דרב, לא רב אמרה, דתיקשי דרב אדרב, אלא מתנית' היא:
Rashi on Eruvin 3a:5:1.english: Rav Yosef said - This amalterah that they brought in the name of Rav is not Rav's own statement, lest Rav be contradicted by Rav; rather, it is a baraita.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:6:1.english: And let it pose a difficulty for Rav - For we see here that the Rabbis did not derive [their ruling] from the Heikhal, since they enacted that the amaltara is effective.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:7:1.english: Remove me from here - Remove me from here, as if I had been silent and had not said this thing.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:7:2.hebrew: מתנייתא מי לא קשיין אהדדי - דהא תניא לעיל בהדיא מבוי שהוא גבוה מכ' יותר מפתחו של היכל, אלמא רבנן מהתם גמרי:
Rashi on Eruvin 3a:7:2.english: Do the baraitot not contradict each other? - For it is explicitly taught above [in a baraita]: an alleyway that is more than twenty [cubits] high exceeds the entrance of the Heikhal. Hence, the Rabbis derive [the measure of twenty cubits] from there.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:7:3.hebrew: תנאי היא - תנא דלעיל דסבירא ליה דרבנן מהיכל גמרי, ואמלתרא לא מהניא, והאי תנא דאמלתרא סבר לאו מהיכל גמרי:
Rashi on Eruvin 3a:7:3.english: It is a tannaitic dispute - The tanna cited above holds that the Rabbis derive [the measurement] from the Heikhal, and the amaltara does not help [to lower it], whereas this tanna who [permits] the amaltara holds that they do not derive [it] from the Heikhal.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:7:4.english: For me too, it is a dispute [between Tannaim] - And I say in accordance with the Tanna cited above.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:8:1.english: Without Rav - If Rav had not explained the first mishna and derived from it that the Rabbis derived [the measurement] from the Heikhal [Temple sanctuary].

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:8:2.english: The mishnayot do not contradict each other - For both that mishna and this mishna [apply to the case of an] amlatera.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:8:3.english: A beam - what is the reasoning of the Rabbis? - They require that it be within twenty cubits.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:8:4.english: Because of the distinguishing mark - So that people will see it and know that a remedy was made, and it will not come to be confused with the public domain [reshut harabim]. Therefore the awning is effective: since people look at it, even above twenty cubits there is a distinguishing mark.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:8:5.english: As for that which it teaches - [In the first baraita, the height is given as] "more than the doorway of the Sanctuary." This is not derived from there. It is merely a mnemonic, so that you do not confuse the reading "twenty" and say "above thirty or forty." Let the doorway of the Sanctuary be a sign in your hand.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:9:1.english: If he holds that of Rabbah - The Rabbis' reasoning applies to a sukkah as well, since it is for the sake of hekker (the requirement that it be recognizable as a sukkah).

Tosafot on Eruvin 3a:18:1.hebrew: אי קלשת הוי לה חמתה מרובה מצילתה - מפר' ר"י חמתה מרובה מצילתה ע"י שיבא הרוח ויפזר עד שתהא חמתה מרובה מצילתה. דאי ע"י קלישה לחודה תהא חמתה מרובה, היכי מכשר' לה בלישנא בתרא? הא אין סכך פסול מצטרף בהדי סכך כשר, כדאמרי' בסוכה (ד' ט:) גבי העושה סוכתו תחת האילן. וקשיא, דאמר בפרק קמא דסוכה (ד' ד.): היתה גבוהה מכ' אמה והוצין יורדין בתוך כ' אם צילתה מרובה מחמתה כשירה, אם לאו פסולה. ואמאי כשירה? והלא אי קלשת ליה, יפלו ההוצין למטה. וללישנא בתרא דהכא אתי שפיר. ולרבא מפרזקיא נמי, דמפרש משום דסוכה דיחיד היא ולא מידכר, אתי שפיר, דגבי הוצין איכא למימר דיורדין הרבה למטה, דליכא למיגזר מידי. אבל לרבינא קשה, דמשמע דמשום סוכה דאורייתא פסולה משום אי קלשת כו'. וי"ל, דהתם מיירי שיש הרבה הוצין שיכולין להתקיים בקל על ידי סמיכה. ועוד, נוכל לומר הכא, דאי קלשת ליה, הוי חמתה מרובה ע"י קלישה לחוד, ומצטרף לסכך דלמעלה מכ'. וללישנא בתרא, דלא חשיב כל כך סכך פסול, הואיל והוי סכך כשר אם היה למטה מכ'. אבל קשה, דגבי הוצין אמרי' ואם לאו פסול, וללישנא בתרא דהכא מכשרינן אפילו חמתה מרובה מצילתה. מיהו ללישנא קמא ניחא. אי נמי, גבי הוצין יש לפסול יותר, הואיל ואגודים עליונים והתחתונים זה בזה, דאי קלשת יפול הכל:
Tosafot on Eruvin 3a:18:1.english: If it is shaken, its sunlight will exceed its shade - R. Yitzchak explains: its sunlight exceeds its shade because the wind will come and scatter it until its sunlight exceeds its shade. For if by shaking alone its sunlight would exceed its shade, how would we validate it according to the latter explanation? Surely invalid schach does not combine with valid schach, as we say in Sukkah 9b concerning one who makes his sukkah under a tree. And it is difficult: in the first chapter of Sukkah (4a) it says that if the sukkah was higher than twenty cubits and hutzin (loose branches) were hanging down within twenty, then if its shade exceeds its sunlight it is kosher, and if not, it is invalid. Why is it kosher? For if you shake it, the hutzin would fall down. According to the latter explanation here, it works out well. And according to Raba of Parzakia as well, who explains that it is a private sukkah and this is not mentioned, it works out well, for regarding hutzin one can say that many of them come down, so there is no need to decree anything. But for Ravina it is difficult, for it implies that a sukkah of Torah law is invalid because 'if you shake it, etc.' One can answer that there it deals with a case where there are many hutzin that can easily remain standing by being propped up. Furthermore, we can say here that if you shake it, its sunlight would exceed its shade through shaking alone, and it combines with the schach above twenty cubits. According to the latter explanation, which does not regard it as so invalid schach, since it would be valid schach if it were below twenty... But it is difficult: regarding hutzin it says 'if not, it is invalid', yet according to the latter explanation here we validate even when its sunlight exceeds its shade. However, according to the first explanation it is fine. Alternatively, regarding hutzin one can disqualify all the more, since the upper and lower bundles are tied to each other, so if one shakes it, everything falls.

Tosafot on Eruvin 3a:22:1.hebrew: אמר רבה במבוי פסול - ל"ג רב, דרב יליף מפתחו של היכל, דהוי חללו כ':
Tosafot on Eruvin 3a:22:1.english: Rabba said: in an invalid mavoi - The reading is not "Rav," for Rav derives [the dimension] from the entrance of the Sanctuary, whose interior was twenty [cubits].

Tosafot on Eruvin 3a:8:1.hebrew: ורב נחמן בר יצחק אי סבירא ליה הא דרבה כו' - לרבה גופיה הוה מצי למיפרך, דאית ליה בפרקין (ד' יב:) דקורה משום היכרא, אלא משום דרב נחמן מפרש בהדיא דפליגי בהיכר; פריך, למה להו לאיפלוגי בתרתי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 3a:8:1.english: And R. Nachman bar Yitzchak, if he holds that [ruling] of Rabbah, etc.? - Rabbah himself could have raised the objection, since he holds in the chapter (ד' יב:) that a beam serves as an identification mark. But since R. Nachman explicitly explains that they disagree about identification, [the Gemara] asks: why would they need to dispute two things?
